title: WoW on the Thor
tagline: World of Warcraft on a handheld: the world up top, bags and map below.
what: The real World of Warcraft, running on the AYN Thor, a handheld built on a phone chip, through a Windows compatibility layer I patched. It plays across both screens, with the game's own windows moved to the touchscreen.
built: Moved WoW's bags, map and quest tracker onto the Thor's touchscreen
My patched Wine build reached the login screen on all 8 cold starts in my test
One 4400 by 1080 canvas shows a different strip on each screen, so WoW thinks it has one monitor
A picker app that starts Retail, Classic or the Forever beta in dual screen

remix.changed: Patched its Wine build and launcher, and added my own dual-screen layout and a picker app.

making.problem: WoW now comes in a version for ARM chips like the Thor's, but nothing I found ran it reliably on a handheld, and the game only knows about one screen.
how: Run it through GameNative's Wine, with the community's ARM64 build of the game.
Use my patched Wine build with ARM64 graphics libraries.
Give Wine one very wide monitor and show different slices of it on each screen, with WoW's own windows moving to the bottom.

proof.caption: Both screens stacked: the world on top, quest tracker, minimap and bags below. An earlier version of the layout.

credits: Runs on: GameNative, Wine, Proton and Mesa Turnip
Controller and dialogue addons: ConsolePort and Immersion by seblindfors
Wine fixes, dual-screen layout, picker app and Thor setup: me
